title: Marvelous Designer Tokyo User Summit 2026 開催のおしらせ
content:

このたび、Marvelous Designerはユーザー参加イベント **「Marvelous Designer Tokyo User Summit 2026」** を開催いたします。

日本での開催は実に4年ぶりです！私たちもこの機会を大変楽しみにしております。

本イベントでは、参加者限定で未公開の新機能をご紹介するほか、Marvelous Designerの開発・運営チームと直接交流いただけます。さらに、ゲーム、アニメーション、映像制作、アパレル、そしてソーシャルVR業界のさまざまな現場で活躍されているMarvelous Designerユーザーの皆様との交流の場もご用意しています。

* * *

## **開催概要**

  * **日時** ：2026年10月27日(火)14:00〜

  * **会場** ：日比谷フォートタワー11階 / 日比谷スカイカンファレンス  
(〒105-0003 東京都港区西新橋1丁目1−1)

  * **参加費** ：無料

  * **参加人数** ：150名(予定)




## **コンテンツ(予定)**

  * Marvelous Designerの活用・成功事例紹介

  * Marvelous Designerチームによる新機能・ロードマップの紹介

  * パートナーセッション

  * ゲスト登壇者セッション

  * ライトニングトークセッション

  * Marvelous Designerチームとのパネルセッション — Ask us anything(質問コーナー)

  * ユーザーアクティビティ

  * 企業・個人ユーザー作品によるアートギャラリー

  * その他お楽しみコンテンツ




※予定内容は現時点のものであり、今後の検討により変更される可能性があります。

* * *

## **参加申し込みフォーム**

参加をご希望の方は、以下の申し込みフォームよりご応募ください。

👉 [**_参加申し込みフォームはこちら_**](https://forms.gle/sw88kKDbyogZwFuY9)

### **参加申し込みに関するご注意**

お申し込みにあたっては同伴者1名様まで （※教育機関 / 企業参加者様の場合は4名様まで）お誘いの上お申し込みいただけます。

当フォームにご記入いただいたご本人様の参加を原則としておりますため、ご参加をご希望の場合は、主となる方に参加申込書をご記入いただくよう、ご案内をお願いいたします。

**2026年9月30日(月)**

### **参加に関するご連絡**

  * 当申し込みフォームのご提出をいただいた参加資格を満たしている方に、当フォーム締め切り後に参加についてのご案内が記載されたメールをお送りさせていただきます。

  * ※大変恐れ入りますが、参加希望者多数の場合はご応募内容をもとに当チームにて人数調整を行わせていただきます。ご参加いただける方へは、案内メールの発送をもってご連絡とさせていただきます。

  * ※当フォームにてご応募いただいた際に記入いただいたメールアドレス宛に、本イベントに関するご案内をお送りいたします。メールアドレスに誤りがないかご確認ください。




### **ご留意事項**

  * ご記入いただいた個人情報は、本サミットの運営にのみ使用し、第三者に提供することはありません。ご登録いただいた方には、Marvelous Designerの今後のイベントや他地域のユーザーサミットに関する情報をお送りする場合があります。

  * イベント中に写真撮影を行います。撮影した写真は当社のマーケティング用途に活用いたしますので、あらかじめご了承ください。




* * *

皆様のご応募を心よりお待ちしております！

title: Marvelous Designer in Game Production: NPC Clothing for Tides of Tomorrow
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/126cb5630ab44e46887077d855f0a5f600_NPC%20-%20%E5%B7%B2%E7%BC%96%E8%BE%91.png)

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PecZgFembb4?start=0

 _Tides of Tomorrow_ is a narrative adventure set in a colorful post-apocalyptic ocean world, where every community needs to feel distinct and alive. For Clothilde Chopin and the DigixArt team, NPC clothing became a key production challenge: creating visual variety at scale while keeping the pipeline efficient and flexible.

In this User Spotlight, Character Artist Clothilde Chopin shares how Marvelous Designer supported the NPC clothing workflow for _Tides of Tomorrow_ , from early garment creation and faction identity to final in-game assets.

**Software used:**

  * Marvelous Designer – Cloth Creation

  * Zbrush – Modeling

  * Maya - Retopology & UV unwrapping

  * Substance Painter – Texturing

  * Unreal Engine - Lighting & Rendering

* * *




# **Could you briefly introduce yourself and your role as a Character Artist at DigixArt on _Tides of Tomorrow_?**

My name is Clothilde Chopin and I’m a French Character Artist working at Digixart Entertainment for 4 years now. I was involved in the creation of the project _Tides of Tomorrow_ from its very beginning right up to its release in April 2026.

Right from the pre-production stage three years ago, I was able to make key decisions regarding the artistic direction of the characters and the setup of our pipeline, taking our technical constraints into account. And throughout production, I created the majority of the characters visible in the game, as well as the clothing library shared by our random NPCs.

# **_Tides of Tomorrow_ has a distinctive plasticpunk world: colorful, oceanic, post-apocalyptic, and shaped by Plastemia. How did this worldbuilding influence your approach to character clothing?**

The impact of our original setting is a reflection we had during the pre-production phase. Very quickly, the choice of having 3 distinct factions differentiated by their clothing style was imposed upon us. So, we had a very large scope for clothing.  
Due to our time constraints and the small size of our team (I was the only character artist for two years!), we opted to use Marvelous Designer in our character workflow.

![4d11e3bee8784e9098a94a72e728fac4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/4d11e3bee8784e9098a94a72e728fac4Cloth_Reclaimers_UE1.jpg)

As we reflected on the game's lore and the inhabitants of this plasticpunk world, several ideas occurred to us regarding how these people might find ways to clothe themselves.

Some, known as "mystics", have managed to develop a way to create their own fabrics from cultivated seaweed fibers. Others, such as "reclaimers," have found ways to recycle plastic materials into clothing. In any case, their garments are not meant to look perfect, like mass-produced factory items with neat, precise stitching. Instead, everything has a patched-together, handmade quality, as if crafted by people with no sewing skills.

![d1dd768ddf2949dcb9e8fdaa8c5f7ab8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/d1dd768ddf2949dcb9e8fdaa8c5f7ab8Cloth_Reclaimers_UE2.jpg)

# **In your NPC clothing pipeline breakdown, you show how costumes were built for a wide range of characters. How did you approach creating a flexible pipeline that could support many NPCs while keeping each one visually distinct?**

To create the greatest possible variety of clothing and avoid obvious repetition among a crowd of characters, one way to cheat is to play with colors. To iterate easily and quickly create variations, each garment is textured within the engine using a shader based on texture masks.

Furthermore, for each garment created in Marvelous, we used Houdini to adapt it to our four body types. Thus, a single item of clothing actually gave dozens of different results in the game. And to ensure that each garment matched the others, they were all imported into a Maya scene, and we adjusted the vertex positions by hand where necessary. The goal was to be able to combine all the clothing items (head, torso, legs, and feet).

**  
![579043008831416faca4951c9c45bd23](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/579043008831416faca4951c9c45bd2300_NPC_reduced.png)**

# **How was Marvelous Designer integrated into your production workflow for _Tides of Tomorrow_? Which parts of the clothing process benefited the most from using it?**

Marvelous is used at the very beginning of the clothing creation pipeline.

During pre-production, that’s where we iterated directly in 3D to test different clothing styles. And during production, that's where clothing assets were created because the sewing pattern modeling system was easy to use. Next, once the base of the garment has been created, it is sent to ZBrush, where the folds are slightly reworked to match the art style and small details such as wear and tear signs and stitching are sculpted. Using Marvelous also benefited UV unwrapping, since the UVs are created based on the pattern.

Our goal was to spend as little time as possible retouching the garment. We therefore made sure to make it as perfect as possible directly within Marvelous.

![9d3b13d9ef634c21b8414a286fa258e0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/9d3b13d9ef634c21b8414a286fa258e0Cloth_Mystic_Shirt_05.JPG)![dd959ef497f54eceafa0a8f795795602](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/dd959ef497f54eceafa0a8f795795602Cloth_Marauder_Shoes_02.jpg)![c75dcef6dfa54ea8b79260ea2086f425](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/c75dcef6dfa54ea8b79260ea2086f425Cloth_Marauder_Jacket_01.jpg)

# **The game features different communities and factions, such as Reclaimers, Marauders, and Mystics. How did you use silhouette, fabric choices, wear, color, and accessories to communicate each group’s identity?**

To preserve the visual identity unique to each faction, we have established material and color references for each of them.

The Mystics use natural materials like seaweed and plants to create fabric for relatively understated, modest outfits; their color palette remains fairly consistent, featuring shades of blue and purple.

![2cd353479c0c42b78183dc4f4ba6f142](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/2cd353479c0c42b78183dc4f4ba6f1422f6d5caf-0dc0-47b6-ad2a-dcbdeccce481.png)

The Reclaimers recycle plastics to create highly colorful garments with rather original and unusual patterns.

![0e21d2f1f3b64e4481556efd5f2518ee](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/0e21d2f1f3b64e4481556efd5f2518ee31cc78f8-4f3e-41ab-8569-bbe1361f42e5.png)

And the Marauders, for their part, obtain their materials from fishing and scrap metal. Their clothing is therefore made of leather and repurposed metal plates. Their color palette is more subdued and darker than that of other communities, featuring shades of dark blue and green, along with red to evoke the rust on the metal.

![c76db131ae2a45099799acc1c38bea9f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/c76db131ae2a45099799acc1c38bea9ff8a4bdba-2817-463c-94a5-7e3fa1d0d460.png)

# **Could you walk us through the process of taking a garment from Marvelous Designer into the final in-game character asset, from simulation and cleanup to texturing, rigging, optimization, or engine integration?**

To create a garment for our game, we start in Marvelous Designer. After importing the base body and (if necessary) solid armatures, we create the garment's primary shapes. Once the silhouette and fold placement look promising, I quadrangulate the mesh, properly position its UVs, and export it to ZBrush (thin and unweld single).

![3be6e5bdd4bd45569b28879ceeff3ab7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/3be6e5bdd4bd45569b28879ceeff3ab7Voot_01_ClothMarvelous.png)  
The first thing I do in ZBrush is assign different polygroups to each part of the garment. I then weld the overlapping vertices and subdivide the mesh so I can work on it properly. Sometimes I smooth out or simplify a few folds if the garment looks too realistic for our art style, but generally, I just get to have fun placing seam lines and details like wear and dirt. I only add thickness to the clothing at the end of the sculpt.

![05077c6bfc6d4064ac48b556d8693553](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/05077c6bfc6d4064ac48b556d8693553Voot_02_ClothRawZbrush.jpg)![2bd468634b7b4b92913bd79a6756d5eb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/2bd468634b7b4b92913bd79a6756d5ebVoot_03_ClothZbrush.jpg)

Next, I send it to Maya for retopology, and I can use the high-poly model to transfer the UVs from the Marvelous mesh onto the new one. Of course, I can tweak them if needed.  
At this stage, the final mesh is sent in parallel to Houdini, where it is morphed to fit other character body shapes, and to Substance Painter, where the high-poly mesh is baked onto the low-poly mesh and then textured.

In reality, since the color and potential texture variations are handled directly within Unreal Engine, black-and-white masks are what get created in Substance Painter. And now, all that's left is to integrate all of that into the engine, and that's it.

![affa1024ab3642fcb878e64b32487fbc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/affa1024ab3642fcb878e64b32487fbcVoot_04_UnrealEngine.png)

# **Since _Tides of Tomorrow_ is a first-person narrative adventure, players often see NPCs up close during dialogue and story moments. How did that affect the level of detail you put into clothing, folds, materials, and character presentation?**

Since _Tides of Tomorrow_ is a first-person game, players view and observe the characters from a very close range. And because it is also a narrative game, they spend most of their time conversing with these characters. So we immediately established that the quality of the characters had to be central to our game.

![5f8419b6d8ab4f23ad77f5e45070f246](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/5f8419b6d8ab4f23ad77f5e45070f2464d5c41df-897e-418f-a4af-47d7e8ed0106.png)

Taking into account the fact that players primarily look at NPCs' faces, we assigned a hierarchy of importance to clothing details. The closer an element is to the face, the more detailed it is. Consequently, the upper body needs to be more visually appealing than the lower body, which is darker and less saturated. To achieve this, we placed great importance on the folds and tension lines of the clothing, because unlike in cinema, these features are baked into the model and not moving and updating in real time.

![9ccfdebd802e422592379008b59946a5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/9ccfdebd802e422592379008b59946a5Efod_02_ClothRawZbrush.jpg)![d8736e98e06e4dd6964fb1a7510075f3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/d8736e98e06e4dd6964fb1a7510075f3Efod_03_UnrealEngine.png)

# **Looking back at character production on _Tides of Tomorrow_ , what was the biggest challenge in building this clothing pipeline, and what advice would you give to character artists who want to use Marvelous Designer in a game production workflow?**

One of the biggest challenges we faced in establishing this pipeline was anticipating quick and effective solutions in case of major changes resulting from production decisions. So we tried to make things as non-destructive and modular as possible.

If I were to offer advice to artists looking to integrate Marvelous Designer into their game production pipeline, I would tell them to carefully establish the workflow between their various 3D software applications so that no effort put into Marvelous goes to waste. Don't hesitate to use zero gravity during Marvelous simulations; this prevents the garment from exhibiting the creases, tension lines, and weight distribution associated with the character's T-pose or A-pose when viewed in the game engine. And one last tip: don't hesitate to seek information from professional tailors, watch tutorials on making real clothes, and look for sewing patterns on specialized websites.

![35c05278f33f44759abad8c671cd4b11](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/9aba618a803e4e5eb7adb3f7ac375ee9/images/35c05278f33f44759abad8c671cd4b11Capture%20d_e%CC%81cran%202024-03-25%20165559.png)

Thank you to those who were curious enough to read my explanations. I hope all of this proves useful for your future projects. Stay curious and have fun exploring different ways to create your 3D clothing. It is, in fact, one of the most important aspect in your character design.

* * *

[Artstation](https://www.artstation.com/fyoston)
content_description: This page showcases how Clothilde Chopin and the DigixArt team used Marvelous Designer and other tools to create a flexible, detailed NPC clothing pipeline that brings unique faction identities to life in the post-apocalyptic world of _Tides of Tomorrow_.

title: Pinch, Rip, Refine. Explore New Features in Marvelous Designer 2026.1
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/448aa11bc06d4b91a63668ca1d12a96e/images/9f91b5d2fb1849c1b8b0c3ab631ba26dSocial%20Media%202026.1%20EN.png)Marvelous Designer 2026.1 delivers a highly anticipated feature you’ve been asking for, and a few more you never knew you needed. Here’s what you’ll find in our latest major update.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hM6viQZeHPI?si=mBr65ZKcFI679sc_

  
**Seamline Ripping Tool [Beta]**

One of our most requested features, the [Beta] Seamline Ripping Tool delivers a powerful new dimension to your toolkit. As the fabric is pulled apart, it will rip just like real fabric, complete with customizable fraying. Use ripping to add dynamism to fights and transformation sequences, and texture to tattered rags and ripped jeans.

  
**Pinching Simulation Override**

The most impactful update to pinching yet, Pinching Simulation Override transforms 3D interaction. Enabling it overrides global fabric and simulation values with your own custom parameters while pinching, giving you precise control over your design in the 3D window. Perfect for creating stylized looks, it allows you to shape your project directly in Marvelous Designer, then lock your changes in place, reducing the need to sculpt in another software.

  
**Brush Pinching**

A brand new type of pinching, Brush Pinching pushes or pulls fabric along a path with a customizable brush. Use it to create precise wrinkles, quickly bunch fabric, and guide movement. Paired with the new Pinching Simulation Override, Brush Pinching is a game-changer for styling garments.

  
**Blend Shape Animation**

Our previous update added blend shape support, which we’re expanding upon with Blend Shape Animation. The ability to add keyframes directly inside Marvelous Designer grants even greater flexibility during animations, faster iterations, more accurate timing control, and simplifies some workflows that previously required morph targets.

  
To learn more about these key features, or about other additions and improvements, visit [_our website_](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/product/newfeature).
content_description: Discover the powerful new features of Marvelous Designer 2026.1, including the Seamline Ripping Tool, enhanced pinching controls, and Blend Shape Animation for more dynamic and precise 3D garment design.

title: Majestic Elegance: Resurrecting the Legacy of Atossa, the Achaemenid Queen 👑
content:
* * *

![7a440c7ccd664bf593c605dd66f3759d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/e2b0023912524a80883757a5e0609f4c/images/7a440c7ccd664bf593c605dd66f3759dATO5.png)![761ea44ec2c846a08e6f0706fcc9a4bc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/e2b0023912524a80883757a5e0609f4c/images/761ea44ec2c846a08e6f0706fcc9a4bc32bac055-c0e1-4115-a7ea-6bb5135abbf3.png)  
Atossa, the daughter of Cyrus the Great, remains one of the most powerful and influential women in ancient history—a true symbol of intellect and Persian imperial grandeur.  
In this digital fashion project, I aimed to capture the magnificent essence of Achaemenid royal attire while adhering to modern 3D industry standards. The ensemble features a heavily textured dark mantle adorned with golden appliqués, a statement belt showcasing the embossed Faravahar emblem, and an intricate geometric crown. The back of the veil is meticulously embroidered with the mythical Homa bird, blending historical motifs with luxury digital fashion.  
Optimized for real-time engines and gaming (Low-Poly), this asset achieves high-fidelity cinematic visuals while maintaining an efficient topology of just 62k triangles.  
💻 **Technical Workflow:**  
Garment Simulation & Pattern: CLO3D  
Retopology & Modeling: Blender  
High-Fidelity Texturing: Substance Painter![e188357e6f584b19974d489f87974f08](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/e2b0023912524a80883757a5e0609f4c/images/e188357e6f584b19974d489f87974f08AR2.png)

title: Evil Jester
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/8b9f618b296b4384ad080548f0f6b9e3sia-melnychenko-jester-opera.jpg)**_From Sewing Machines to Marvelous Designer: How Think Tank Graduate_**[** _Sia Melnychenko_**](https://www.artstation.com/melantasy)** _Merges Her Lifelong Passion for Sewing with MD to Create High-End Characters._**

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c1DXeq8A6bI

**Software Used:**

  * Zbrush - Blockout, Sculpting

  * Marvelous Designer - Garment Creation

  * Maya - Retopology, UV-unwrapping, xGen Interactive Groom

  * Marmoset Toolbag - Baking

  * Substance Painter - Texturing

  * Unreal Engine - Character Setup(simulations, physics), Lighting & Rendering




# **Could you briefly introduce yourself and tell us about the "Evil Jester" project?**

My name is Sia and I’ve been learning 3D Character Art for 3 years. I was always into arts and crafts, but I was also a big fan of video-games. I think deep down I always knew what I wanted to do for work: growing up one of my favorite games was The Sims 2, where I’d always spend hours creating characters. At some point I even discovered The Sims 2 Body Shop and started redrawing textures in Paint to create custom clothing pieces.

I started thinking about doing 3D around 2019, but I had too many excuses - my ancient laptop won’t boot up Maya, I was a full-time student with a job, etc. So after I got laid off from my recruiter job in late 2022 I knew it was time to finally focus on something I really wanted. It’s 2026 and I have never looked back ever since. I have worked on a mobile RPG game in a small company for nearly two years, where I learned a lot of technical stuff and optimization. Now, after graduating from Think Tank, my main goal is to transition into a PC/Console space and join a company where I can use my skillset to create a game that hopefully inspires other people just like I was inspired by some of my favorite titles.

[Evil Jester](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/41be9n) was meant to be the crown jewel of my time at Think Tank. I had very high hopes for the project: I wanted to develop complex cloth elements, include armor pieces, and have a visually interesting character with a lot of accessories.

![9af15c0bb0e24aa3a9b1698ad9e02ddc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/9af15c0bb0e24aa3a9b1698ad9e02ddcEvilJester.jpg)

I didn’t settle on the concept art until the very last minute, since nothing ticked all of my boxes. I do have a strict rule when it comes to choosing a concept art - I have to love it. I came across “Jester” by Dariya R on Pinterest and it was love at first sight. I didn’t even run it by my mentor first, I was so certain that the concept was “it”. I just started the blockout that same day just so he can’t say no to me.

# **You mentioned that your lifelong passion for sewing makes you look forward to the garment creation stage in MD. For artists without a sewing background, what do you think is their biggest hurdle when learning MD, and how could MD features make cloth-making even more intuitive for them?**

Sewing is an incredibly rewarding craft - you get to actually experience your fruit of labor. I always gravitated towards sewing machines, watched sewing content and tried to do a little sewing myself - I made toys and outfits for dolls.

When I got to experience Marvelous Designer for the first time I was blown away - I can create outfits for my characters using actual patterns and sewing techniques?! It took some adjusting for sure, but it still brings me as much joy as it did when I first launched the software.  
![f383e13f61e44485bb250feba3d9d52a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/f383e13f61e44485bb250feba3d9d52aPreviousProjects-MD.jpg)

For those who are not as “in the theme” of sewing I’m sure Marvelous Designer can be frustrating at first. But there’s nothing a simple pattern from the web can’t fix. For most use cases there will be a real life counterpart that has a pattern. As with anything else in 3D - it’s always great to have references.

While working with people who are less comfortable with MD I noticed that they’re afraid to be creative - in order to achieve your vision you need to drastically modify patterns, cut, stitch, create darts, try out different fabrics for their simulation properties, etc. The 3D viewport tells the story perfectly - it’s easy to see where I need to take the fabric in, and where to add. Some also overlook Curve Tools, which in my opinion are essential if you're trying to get a good fitting garment.

![2949d31a35fb4f7a8cfcce62bbbfadb7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/2949d31a35fb4f7a8cfcce62bbbfadb7ezgif-894509ae62a72e4b.gif)

And another small piece of advice I can give is watching sewing videos. If your goal is to understand how it all works and get more savvy - that’s the best way. Sometimes if you’re making a difficult garment it’s important to know the right order of manipulations, and how are you supposed to know this if you’re never seen it done? I think that seeing how it’s done in real life gives you a better insight on how pattern creation works, attaching more meaning to the pixel patterns on the screen.

![98eb40ef3fef4e8da696fce20e85b1e3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/98eb40ef3fef4e8da696fce20e85b1e3EvilJester-Final.jpg)

# **You highlighted Freeze and Solidify as 'game changers' during your 'Evil Jester' project. Could you walk us through a specific part of that garment where these tools saved time or enabled a complex design?**

Evil Jester’s outfit featured the classic “Jester sleeves”, as well as the dress-like vest with lacing at the front. It was rather important for me to try and preserve the distinct shapes of these two elements.

I always start with blocking inside of ZBrush, it provides a pretty solid base for what I have in mind. In Marvelous, I like to start from a blank canvas with my avatar and work on patterns, see how it looks and then go from there.I did an extensive research into the jester fashion and was lucky to find some actual patterns that looked promising.

I think that every garment I create in Marvelous Designer opens up new tools that make the process exponentially more satisfying. While working on Evil Jester I found my newest helper: I would paint a part of my garment that I want to freeze or solidify - and that really helped me achieve the best shape possible.

![86efe0712397443ba919718081b5bee9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/86efe0712397443ba919718081b5bee9EvilJester-Freeze-01.jpg)

Another trick I found helpful is creating an internal line a few millimeters from the edge, cutting it off and freezing (or solidifying). This trick is helpful for the situations where you want to try to keep the shape but also let the simulation do its magic.

![929c1c7344da4e42b05f41be42f3567a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/929c1c7344da4e42b05f41be42f3567aEvilJester-Freeze-02.jpg)

Another way I use freeze is cutting my patterns in a smart way. For jester sleeves it proved very helpful because I could focus on one segment at a time, making sure everything looks exactly as I want.

![ace1fb12ec7e400e9e8d6bdc9f05083c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/ace1fb12ec7e400e9e8d6bdc9f05083cEvilJester-Freeze-03.jpg)

# **You mentioned converting custom 3D models into garments using UV unwrapping as a pattern. How does this technique fit into your overall pipeline alongside other 3D software?**

When I created Jester’s vest in Marvelous Designer, the skirt would flop down and won’t hold the shape at all. Since I knew exactly how I wanted it to look, I took my ZBrush sculpt, UV unwrapped it in Maya to resemble an actual pattern and brought it to MD. From there I spent some time cleaning up, since converted patterns often come with a huge amount of curve points that will hinder any tweaking of the pattern. I only wanted to use the skirt, since I was pleased with the top part of the vest. I stitched my MD pattern with my blockout pattern, solidified the skirt to preserve the shape + manually painted some freeze zones where it was crucial to keep the shape intact. One side of the vest also features a torn edge that was created with curve points, but I decided to create a cleaned up version with an untorn edge for an easier retopology process.  
![51163703a16d4cecb372c21a8afd6144](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/51163703a16d4cecb372c21a8afd6144EvilJester-MeshToGarment-Vest.jpg)  
![24704e99e85c48868bc61cf08d8424e7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/24704e99e85c48868bc61cf08d8424e7ezgif-416f6c88caacf14b.gif)

I also used the same pipeline for boots. They’re made from thick leather and I probably could’ve sculpted everything manually, but I wanted to try and see, so I did the same thing - ZBrush sculpt, Maya UVs and then Marvelous Designer for simulation. I made sure to freeze the bottom part of the boot where it tightly hugs the foot, since the simulation wasn’t required there. I really appreciate the wide variety of premade fabrics that MD provides - it helps immensely with simulations. I always make sure to use Full Trim Leather or Hard Trim Fabric for such elements, where I don’t want to get an excessive amount of wrinkles. I enjoy this approach and use it where I can because it can save a lot of time in the prototyping stage, and combined with a solid knowledge of patterns you can achieve a very clean result.   
![e62a8d9beb534355a16aa2d7deeb822e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/e62a8d9beb534355a16aa2d7deeb822eEvilJester-MeshToGarment-Boots.jpg)I really liked the idea of having a luxurious looking cape, and Marvelous Designer yet again ended up being the best solution. The free-flowing part simulated perfectly and it never changed much past the initial pattern, meanwhile the top part had plenty of manual sculpting involved to make it align with the concept art. I think I ended up with a perfectly balanced garment, plus on top of everything I was able to simulate it beautifully inside of Unreal Engine, which adds so much realism to the character.

  
![836b70b3708f4a499bfb2c9045000ce5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/836b70b3708f4a499bfb2c9045000ce5EvilJester-Cape.jpg)

Marvelous Designer is an essential part of character creation in my opinion - creating realistic garments is very difficult and MD makes this process so much more satisfying. I always trust the process and try to preserve as many details as possible, so the garment is still recognizable in its final form, despite going through so many stages.**  
![a715d6077bd94949be187722ac199f48](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/a715d6077bd94949be187722ac199f48EvilJester-Details.jpg)![5fda2b1e4c244aa7b556829d06c2cd41](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/5fda2b1e4c244aa7b556829d06c2cd41EvilJester-Texturing.jpg)**

# **Having used MD for 2.5 years, you’ve seen significant software updates. Which feature addition over this period had the most positive impact on your daily workflow?**

I used to only stitch my patterns in a 2D viewport, I can’t really tell if the 3D version wasn’t reliable or I just never quite figured it out since I was comfortable with the “classic version”. But recently I saw someone stitch in the 3D viewport and it worked so well, I just had to implement it in my personal workflow!

3D Pen is also my absolute go to in every project - It’s so convenient to use when you want to prototype a pattern and get exact measurements from the avatar. It saves a lot of time and gives you a great base to work with.  
![731def48a6634a7cbf7577cda90d549d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/731def48a6634a7cbf7577cda90d549dezgif-451af330062c3730.gif)

The Sculpt Tool is great for adding final touches to the garments. I find it most helpful as the final step, where I can slightly “edit” my pattern and nudge it in place or add a wrinkle I had in mind. Sadly, if you try to simulate the garment afterwards it will disappear altogether, but as a final touch it’s unbeatable!![5a71e1d4d5b84c0b9cf08ba06f59648c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/5a71e1d4d5b84c0b9cf08ba06f59648cezgif-4a0ea786e1db9148.gif)

Another thing that is not often mentioned in any pipelines or tutorials is the option to convert pattern topology from triangles to optimized quads. I used to manually retopologize all of my MD garments before using them in the highpoly stage, but with the addition of optimized quad geometry I don’t really see the reason to do it anymore, only for specific patterns that end up requiring extra love.  
![aee608e72bc34e8087078244cc36dbc0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/693d6a4bdefe48ca871a21e3687f1c09/images/aee608e72bc34e8087078244cc36dbc0ezgif-412040746cf99a8a.gif)

I also appreciate that nowadays I can effectively use the GPU mode in Marvelous as it now works as good as the CPU counterpart. It used to be different and the simulation was worse, but now it’s perfect and allows me to do more without any performance issues.

title: Strange brain-y texture
content:
I uploaded a custom model, converted it into an avatar but also tested clothing on the base obj file as well as the avatar. The clothing looks really strange on this model when I do auto fitting or manual fitting. It creates this strange brain-y look. As soon as I hit simulate it always gets me this weird look on the clothing. I tried changing particle distance and a few other things but I haven't seen others with this same issue. I tried this with different clothes and it seemed consistent with my specific model. Other models turned out fine, you can see the basic green shirt was fine on the default avatar.

![aa694ecde0eb4a67a7872f07422804f4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/3fc9a7ce0f164836bf715db65d8ac73d/images/aa694ecde0eb4a67a7872f07422804f41.webp)![57c8cb29376b41e9ab047ccf25f2ee9f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/3fc9a7ce0f164836bf715db65d8ac73d/images/57c8cb29376b41e9ab047ccf25f2ee9f2.webp)![2db8595675344053888e1e8662790fa6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/3fc9a7ce0f164836bf715db65d8ac73d/images/2db8595675344053888e1e8662790fa63.webp)![0583fcd550244789bc988f8aa30eebee](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/3fc9a7ce0f164836bf715db65d8ac73d/images/0583fcd550244789bc988f8aa30eebee4.webp)
